scope: S5 Tool broker recovery on exclusive disposable PostgreSQL and MinIO. The fixture adapter records application acceptance of the runtime-owned operation ID, then simulates process loss before the worker can persist an outcome or acknowledge its lease. It is not a Workspace service, protected sandbox, Firecracker, or Linux/KVM execution claim.

observations.initial_effect: A real broker Worker consumed the approved one-use grant, persisted the execution intent and claim, and supplied the exact runtime Operation ID to the external-effect fixture before the simulated worker loss.
observations.recovery: After the ten-second claim lease expired, a fresh PostgreSQL pool and StateRuntime reopened the durable state. The replacement Worker called only Reconcile with the same persisted Operation ID and made no Execute call.
observations.uncertainty: The status-only adapter returned an unknown result. The worker persisted ToolExecutionUncertain, retained no Artifact/result, and the owner-scoped public Tool projection and finalization event exposed only the safe uncertain terminal outcome.
observations.audit: The retained correlated terminal audit fact and outbox route remain ordered and contain no descriptor credential-shaped value or external backend handle.

redaction: No DSNs, object-store credentials, raw tenant/session/turn/grant/operation IDs, descriptor bytes, input bytes, artifact body, backend endpoint, or provider credential are retained.
